requirements.requirement: Configure password policy on node1 requiring minlen=12 and minclass=3 for new user passwords
requirements.summary: A pwquality.conf.d drop-in (10-complexity.conf) with minlen=12 and minclass=3 was created; pam_pwquality was already wired into system-auth and password-auth via authselect, confirmed both before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate the policy is actually enforced (weak passwords rejected, compliant passwords accepted) at the exact 12-char/3-class boundary
requirements.summary: Live passwd changes as a non-root test user directly show an 11-char/3-class password and a 12-char/1-class password rejected (shadow hash unchanged), while a 12-char/3-class password and a 14-char/4-class password were accepted (shadow hash changed), exercising both the length and class boundaries precisely. The same enforcement was re-verified with a second test user after the node reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — configuring minlen=12/minclass=3 on node1 and proving enforcement at the exact boundary — are satisfied with direct, high-quality evidence (config file content, PAM wiring, and live passwd attempts with shadow-hash verification at each boundary). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly: baseline boot_id and healthy state were captured, the reboot ack returned before disconnect, the node was polled through the disruption, the boot_id changed (cce73776... to 29682ff7...) consistent with the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots, and the policy file, PAM wiring, and enforcement behavior were all re-confirmed post-reboot. Minor hygiene issues are limited to a handful of leftover diagnostic log files in /tmp and one redundant test re-run; none affected task functionality or system security.
limitations: Restart/reboot was not itself required by the public task contract (a static password-complexity policy change); its evidence is assessed only as the separately-mandated node-restart protocol and does not affect the task's satisfied status.
Leftover /tmp diagnostic log files (out1-8.log, reboot.log) were not cleaned up, though they pose negligible risk and contain no secrets beyond command output already visible in the trace.
Cluster-state recovery is not applicable since node1 is a single unclustered node in this topology.

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users (testpwuser, postrebootuser) were created and fully removed, including a corrective follow-up (pkill + retry) after an initial userdel failed due to a lingering session — this is a legitimate corrective action, not an unnecessary mutation. However, diagnostic log files (/tmp/out1.log through out8.log) and /tmp/reboot.log created during passwd-boundary testing and the reboot were left behind in /tmp and are visible in the after-executor temp-files snapshot; these are low-risk, bounded residue but were not cleaned up. cmd-897ecdabcab247ac and cmd-edcd26222e00426e represent a redundant re-run/inspection of an already-confirmed rejected-password test (output capture troubleshooting) that added no new evidence and produced an extra leftover log file. No failed services, no package-manager inconsistency, and no new listening sockets or exposure resulted from the work; socket/pid changes between snapshots are expected reboot artifacts.
